## Active

### D-002 — A legacy memory file is refused until it is migrated

> _2026-09-15 · tools/blong-dev · active_

add, close, move, index and format refuse a file that has no generated index block, because an
inserted entry would land next to prose the parser cannot describe. check stays permissive so it can
report what a legacy file still needs.

### D-003 — Package memory files must stay tracked by git

> _2026-09-15 · tools/blong-dev · active_

The repository .gitignore ignores a bare todo.md, which also matched the package memory todo files:
migrated package todos were untracked and would never have been committed. The memory paths are
negated explicitly; keep that negation when the ignore rules change.

### D-066 — blong-dev sql falls back to the shared adapter's dev defaults

> _2026-08-21 · tools/blong-dev · active_

`blong-dev sql` failed with `Access denied for user ''@'...'` when `.blong_devrc` did not configure
a `srv.db` connection (the repo-root file only has `db.sql` for a remote ut-microservice database
and `_srv.db._google`), which forced `kubectl exec` into the MySQL pod: `readConnection` resolved to
`{}` and mysql2 connected as an anonymous user. `readConnection` now starts from the shared `srv.db`
adapter's dev defaults (`blong-admin`/`password` at `localhost:3306`) when resolving the default
`srv.db` key and layers `.blong_devrc` plus CLI overrides on top, with missing fields keeping the
defaults; custom `--config` keys stay empty when unconfigured, which preserves the
`--config mysql.sql` test. An `ensureDatabase` helper and a `derived` flag auto-create the derived
dev database (`${suite}-${user}`) when it is missing, mirroring the dev intent's
`createDatabase: true`. The `srv.db`-only fallback was chosen over applying defaults to every key
(which would break the custom-key contract), and auto-create applies only to the DERIVED database,
never to an explicit `--database`. Verified: 44/44 tap tests (13 sql tests including four new),
`tsc --noEmit` green, and a live run that auto-created `blong-access-kalin`.

### D-067 — blong-dev sql always allows multiple statements

> _2026-08-21 · tools/blong-dev · active_

Asked to run several `;`-separated statements in one query and return all their results, the command
now always enables mysql2's `multipleStatements: true`. With it, a single statement's result comes
back as-is (a rows array or a `ResultSetHeader`) while multiple statements are collected into an
ARRAY of result sets; `isMultiResult` detects the shape (an array whose every element is an array or
a `fieldCount`-bearing header) and `formatResultSet` renders it. JSON output emits a single result
set unchanged, keeping it backward compatible, or the array of result sets for multi; pretty output
labels each set `— result N`. Verified: 84/84 tap tests, `tsc --noEmit` green, and live runs showing
`[[rows],[rows]]` for two selects and `[header, header, [rows]]` for create/insert/select.

### D-001 — Memory files are written through blong-dev memory

> _2026-09-15 · tools/blong-dev · active_

The three root memory files (about 3050 lines) were slow to search and referenced each other by line
number. Every entry now has a stable id (one per kind, numbered in writing order), a
`date · area · status` meta line, a section that matches its status and a place in a generated index
at the top of the file, so an agent reads about 40 lines instead of a whole file. Package-specific
entries move to the package's `.github/memory/`; the root keeps cross-cutting, ci, docs and skills.

### D-195 — blong-dev log reads the record shape, payloads behind a flag

> _2026-09-17 · tools/blong-dev · active_

`blong-dev log` reads the store in the record shape the semantic logger writes, and hides payload
blobs unless `--payloads` is given, rather than trying to read both shapes. Records are located
through `service` and `context` (which the condensed line prints as the component), `operation`
(printed as the method) and `refs.trace` (printed as the trace id), so its `--name`, `--method` and
`--trace-id` filters work against what the logger actually writes. The existing cache was deleted
when this landed, because its entries were written in the pino shape and nothing reads them any
more.

### D-247 — blong-dev test gives tap 180 seconds, not 30

> _2026-09-21 · tools/blong-dev · active_

`blong-dev test` passes `--timeout=180` to tap unless the invocation sets `--timeout` itself,
because tap's 30s default is smaller than the fixed startup of an integration entry point (13.5s of
`load()` in a 26s file).

The narrower alternative — setting the timeout in each realm's `ci-test` script — was rejected: the
cost is the runtime's `load()`, which every package's tap entry point pays, so the budget is a
property of the runner rather than of a package. It is also the same place the runner already adds
`--allow-incomplete-coverage` and `--coverage-report=none`.

180s rather than 60s because tap hands the same number to the child as its per-test timeout, so this
is a ceiling for a genuine hang rather than a budget a suite approaches; the measured need is 26s,
and CI runs two packages in parallel.

### D-273 — A run is either watched or captured, and the report is the captured one

> _2026-09-26 · tools/blong-dev · active_

A tap run has one reporter, so `blong-dev test` cannot print live output and write the structured
JSON report at the same time. The split is therefore a choice made per run, not a layer on top.

A watched run (a dev run, unless `--report` is passed) keeps tap's own reporter and relays it as it
arrives. That is what tells a person something is happening: a step is visible while it runs instead
of appearing at the end with its duration, which is exactly when a step that waited too long for
something is noticeable. The relayed stream is written to `tap.raw.tap`, which is the machine
readable artifact of a watched run, and no `report.json` is written — the note the run prints says
so.

A captured run (CI, or `--report` in dev) asks tap for the structured report with `--reporter-file`,
so the tool never holds it, keeps the raw stream as an artifact with `--output-file`, and prints
only the failure view. `report.json` and `summary.md` are a captured run's contract.

This supersedes the earlier idea of echoing a buffered artifact after a json run: the json report
does not contain the test process's own records, and an echo at the end is exactly the "nothing
seems to be happening" a long run was complained about for.

### D-274 — Allure producers write their own results and blong-dev merges them

> _2026-09-26 · tools/blong-dev · active_

A package can report to Allure from more than one producer — a realm's browser tests and its handler
tests — so the question was to merge them or to keep two reports. Merging won, because the CI report
links one report per package and Allure's trend history is kept per package: two reports would have
meant two links, two history slices and two trend lines to keep in step.

The producers do not share a results directory. Each one clears the directory it writes to before a
run, so sharing would make the published report depend on the order the producers ran in, with the
earlier one's results erased. `allure-results` is the browser reporter's and `allure-results-tap` is
the handler tests'.

The merge is one function, `publishAllureReport` in `tools/blong-dev/src/report/allurePublish.ts`,
called by both commands that can be a package's last producer: the tap runner and the browser one.
It stages every results directory that holds anything, moves the trace archives out of the
single-file report into the published `traces/`, hands Allure the package's history slice, and
copies the generated `index.html` and `summary.json` into `.ci-report/publish/` — copying rather
than replacing the directory, so a later producer's run merges instead of deleting what is already
published.

Each result says which producer wrote it (`source: handler-test` from this side), which is what a
reader filters on inside the one document. The framework config no longer asks for a generated
report in CI: the publisher owns generation, and generating inside the test process would have
written a report nobody uploads.

### D-275 — Allure publish is gated on fresh results, not on results

> _2026-09-26 · tools/blong-dev · active_

The Allure publish step is gated on a producer having written results *since* the published report,
rather than on results merely being present.

Without the gate, every `blong-dev test` in a package that had ever run a browser suite regenerated
a full Allure report: `allure-results` is left behind by whichever browser run happened last, and it
is non-empty, so the merge had something to render every time. In this repository that is every
realm, demo and suite, which turned a zero-cost step into seconds of Allure per handler-test run —
and published a stale run as if it were the current one.

What triggers the regeneration is any producer being newer than the published `index.html`; what is
merged is every producer that has results, because the producers of one cycle do not write at the
same moment: the handler-test run publishes first and the browser run that follows has to merge what
is already there.

### D-285 — report.json is a package's report, not a runner's

> _2026-09-26 · tools/blong-dev · active_

A package's .ci-report/report.json describes the package, so it is written one runner's slice at a
time: a producer that is going to report clears its own slice before its run starts (clearRun) and
writes it when the run finishes (writeRun), where IRunReport is one runner's results, IReport.runs
holds every runner of the cycle and IReport.counts is their sum with the status being the worst run.
The clear happens before the run rather than after it so a run that dies mid-way cannot leave the
previous report of that runner to be aggregated as the current one, and only a run that will report
clears anything: a watched dev run writes no report, so it must not clear the slice of the last
captured cycle, and a caller that supplies its own tap reporter owns reporting entirely. Clearing is
runner-scoped because the directory also holds the published Allure report and the browser leg's
trend history, which the blanket .ci-report wipe in blong-dev test deleted — that wipe was the
second half of the bug and is gone. Everything read from the report follows the same rule: a
two-runner package gets a runner table and a Runner-column problem list in summary.md, its failing
tests are attributed to the runner that produced them in the aggregate report, and ci-summary.json
and failures.json carry runners per package plus runner per failure but no singular package runner,
because that field could only ever describe one of the legs.

### D-286 — The CI report prints only what it can prove

> _2026-09-26 · tools/blong-dev · active_

The report gained five stats, each derived from data the runners were already writing: the runner
split (per package in its row, summed in a line above the table), test time (per package, per run
and the five slowest tests), skipped and todo tests, coverage movers against the baseline, and where
each failure stands in the base branch's history. Nothing is invented: a runner that reported no
duration contributes zero and stays out of the slowest lists, a package the baseline never measured
gets no mover row, and a section with nothing to say is not rendered at all. Failure provenance is
deliberately a hint, not a verdict, because only a name joins a report entry to a history record:
Allure's result id changes between runs of the same test, so fullName is the only stable identity,
and the two producers do not even share a separator (the browser leg writes file › suite › title,
the handler leg realm.collection.group.step). The index normalises both into one segment list,
matches suffixes with an exact full name first, and drops a name that two tests of one package claim
in one run rather than guessing, which is why ITestEntry now carries the producer's fullName.
Durations are summed per package rather than overlapped, because a package's legs run one after the
other, so the number is test time and not the wall clock of a CI job. Declined: a run-health streak
from the baseline history, and a duration trend in the committed metrics.json — the duration numbers
live in report.json and ci-summary.json instead, so the committed baseline schema stays as it is.

### D-287 — A number and its delta share one cell

> _2026-09-26 · tools/blong-dev · active_

The CI report's stats live in the cell of the measurement they belong to, rather than in columns or
tables of their own: the Total cell carries the test delta, the Duration cell carries the time delta
and, when the package owns one of the run's five slowest tests, a ⏱️ mark with that test and its
time, and the Coverage cell carries the percentage-point delta plus a direction mark — 🟢 for any
gain, 🔴 for a loss of more than a point, 🟡 for a smaller loss, and no mark when coverage did not
move or there is no baseline to compare against, since a mark that says which way cannot be drawn
for a number that stayed put. The separate Δ Tests column, the Slowest tests table and the Coverage
movers table are gone; the ranked data they held is still in ci-summary.json as coverageMovers and
per-package durationMs, so nothing was lost for an agent. The slowest test is marked in the duration
cell because the timeout budget is per test, and the row that has the time is where a reader looks
for the reason; a test name in a cell is cut at 48 characters so a long generated name cannot
stretch the table. The prose above the table keeps only what no row can say: the package count and
the run's total test time (with its own delta, which needs metrics.json to carry tests.durationMs),
the split by runner, and the comparison with the last merged main. That durationMs field is the one
schema addition this needed: it is optional, so a baseline committed before it simply has no
duration delta and the report states the time alone rather than inventing a comparison.

## Superseded

### D-270 — A watched test run echoes tap, a captured one does not

> _2026-09-26 · tools/blong-dev · superseded_

A run of `blong-dev test` prints two different things depending on whether its output is watched or
captured, and the reporter is not what decides it.

tap is always asked for its structured report and told to write it straight to `tap.json` with
`--reporter-file`, so the tool never holds the report in memory. The raw TAP stream goes to
`tap.raw.tap` with `--output-file`. That stream is the only artifact carrying the test process's own
records — the framework logs a suite prints — because tap's JSON report does not include them, which
was the real cause of the "CI got quieter, and so did dev" report: the tool was reading stdout into
a string and forwarding nothing but stderr.

A captured run (CI) keeps both artifacts and prints only the failure view. A watched run echoes the
raw stream as the file grows, so a dev terminal shows the framework's records and tap's own view
again. The echo is driven by `CI`, in `shouldEchoRawTap`, so a pipeline or an agent still gets the
failure view and the artifacts without a wall of TAP.

Superseded: the echoed-artifact design is gone. A watched run now keeps tap's own live reporter and
writes its stream to tap.raw.tap; the structured report belongs to a captured run.
